A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe the same SceneBench and Scene-RAG study, including Appendices A–H. Text and visual inspection support full comparison; pages 2–16 are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, retrieval comparisons, and component ablations in Section 5, plus frame-length, runtime, and hyperparameter analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results in Section 5 and the appendices, including benchmark scores, ablations, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same Scene-RAG procedure: TV-L1 scene tiling, multimodal memory construction, query decomposition, and retrieval. No algorithm component or model procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six SceneBench tasks and retain the Video-MME and MLVU experiments. No dataset, domain, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated models in Table 2 are unchanged. Tables 3–4 retain the same non-RAG and Video-RAG comparisons against Scene-RAG for LongVA, Long-LLaVA, and LLaVA-OneVision.

E3.justification: Section 5 and the appendices retain identical frame counts, model sizes, evaluation metrics, retrieval settings, and experimental configurations. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 5, frame-length analysis in Figure 5, runtime analysis in Table 7, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis in Table 8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Dataset descriptive statistics and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported scores, trends, and appendix results are unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports LongVA averages of 53.3 without RAG and 54.4 with Scene-RAG in both versions.

T1.justification: The TV-L1 objective in Equation (1), scene-detection threshold, and mathematical definitions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about SceneBench, long-context forgetting, and Scene-RAG's benefits. Contribution scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of forgetting and audio/retrieval benefits are unchanged, as are the appendix discussions of computational constraints, limited hyperparameter exploration, and annotation ambiguity.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime information remain identical. The dataset link and code/data release statements are unchanged; the contact email also remains the same.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix D, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to earlier benchmarks and retrieval methods changes.

P1.justification: v3 identifies Chao Li as corresponding author using a dagger and new footnote, and replaces 'Correspondence to' with 'Contact' before the same email address. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added author superscript and corresponding-author footnote produce a small first-page layout adjustment. All figures and tables retain their designs and contents, and pages 2–16 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies corresponding-author labeling and updates the version stamp, with minor first-page reflow. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and complete appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
